title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous page). 𝒢 is a profinite group containing a normal copy of Ĝ⁺_{0,3}. This is very likely the profinite completion of PSL2(Z) ≅ Z/2 * Z/3, generated by σ (σ²=1) and ρ (ρ³=1), with ε0 = σρ and ε1 = ρσ. 𝒢 acts on it by conjugation. 𝒢[0] ⊂ 𝒢 is the subgroup of elements u0 that send ρ and σ to conjugates of themselves: u0(ρ) = int(α0)ρ and u0(σ) = int(β0)σ. This defines two 'cocycles' α0, β0 : 𝒢[0] → Ĝ⁺_{0,3}. This is the PSL2-form of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type action, where (λ, f) acts on Ĝ_{0,3}.

Grothendieck now takes a continuous surjection φ : 𝒢 → M, with 𝔾 = φ(Ĝ⁺_{0,3}) and M[0] = φ(𝒢[0]). He sets α = φ(α0(u0)) and β = φ(β0(u0)). The question is whether these induce maps defined on M[0] itself.

Step 1 (16)–(17). In M one has αρα⁻¹ = uρu⁻¹ for u = φ(u0). Equivalently [α,ρ] = αρ(α)⁻¹ = [u,ρ], where ρ(α) denotes ρ acting by inner conjugation; likewise for β and σ. Hence α⁻¹u lies in T_ρ = Centr_M(ρ) and β⁻¹u lies in T_σ = Centr_M(σ). So modulo T_ρ (resp. T_σ), α and β depend only on u.

Step 2: the hypothesis. α and β should depend only on u = φ(u0), not on the lift u0. To make this explicit, set J = Ker(𝒢[0] → M[0]) and compare u0 with u0' = δ0·u0, δ0 ∈ J. The crossed-homomorphism rule α(gh) = g(α(h))·α(g), which follows from composing the conjugation actions, gives α0' = δ0(α0)·ᾱ0, where ᾱ0 = α0(δ0); the same holds for β.

Step 3. Apply φ. Since φ(δ0) = 1, one has φ(δ0(α0)) = φ(α0) = α. This gives (19): α' = α·ᾱ and β' = β·β̄ in 𝔾. So the hypothesis is equivalent to (20): for every δ0 ∈ J, α0(δ0) and β0(δ0) lie in Ker φ.

Outcome (next page). When (20) holds, α and β factor through maps M[0] ⇉ 𝔾 satisfying u(ρ) = int(α)ρ and u(σ) = int(β)σ. Writing ξ = [u,ρ] and η = [u,σ], one gets ξ = η·t1^ν with ν = (μ−1)/2, where μ is the multiplier, assumed to factor through M.

Purpose. To pass from the profinite 'big' group to arbitrary (e.g. finite) quotients M while keeping the GT-type cocycle data, i.e. to define a 'GT-like structure' on a quotient. This is part of the 'variations sur l'équation des lacets' that follow La Longue Marche.
errors: Minor: α0 and β0 are a priori only defined modulo the centralizer of ρ (resp. σ) in Ĝ⁺_{0,3}, i.e. modulo ⟨ρ⟩ (resp. ⟨σ⟩). The cocycle identity α0' = δ0(α0)ᾱ0 holds exactly only after a normalization that is not stated on this page; otherwise it holds only modulo these centralizers.
In (20) the condition really means α0(δ0), β0(δ0) ∈ Ker φ ∩ Ĝ⁺_{0,3} (Ker of φ restricted to Ĝ⁺_{0,3}), since α0 and β0 take values there; the page writes simply 'Ker φ'. This is harmless.
The argument in step 1 gives dependence on u only modulo T_ρ ∩ 𝔾 (resp. T_σ ∩ 𝔾), not the full centralizer in M. This is implicit and harmless.

ideas.what: Elements of the 'outer' group 𝒢[0] act on the profinite free product Z/2*Z/3 by sending ρ and σ to conjugates; the conjugators form crossed homomorphisms α, β with the GT-type relation ξ = η t1^{(μ−1)/2}.
ideas.modern_name: Action of GT-type groups / Galois on π1 of M_{1,1}, i.e. the profinite completion of PSL2(Z); the GT 'two-cell' relation in PSL2 form
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990), Ihara; Lochak–Schneps for the PSL2/SL2 formulations
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (Teichmüller tower, T̂_{1,1}) in spirit; La Longue Marche (unpublished)

ideas.what: Descent criterion: the cocycles descend from 𝒢[0] to a quotient M[0] iff α(J), β(J) ⊂ Ker φ, with J = Ker(𝒢[0] → M[0]).
ideas.modern_name: Descent of crossed homomorphisms to quotients; compatibility of a GT-type action with a normal subgroup (cf. 'GT-shadows' for finite quotients)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard group cohomology; for GT on finite quotients: Dolgushev and coauthors (GT-shadows, c. 2021–)

ideas.what: Ambiguity of the conjugator measured by centralizers T_ρ, T_σ in the quotient M.

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up a systematic way to push the GT/Galois-type cocycle data (α, β, multiplier) down to arbitrary profinite quotients M of the ambient group, with an explicit compatibility condition on the kernel. This is close in spirit to the recent 'GT-shadows' programme, which approximates GT by data on finite quotients. Here it is done in the PSL2(Z) = Z/2*Z/3 presentation rather than F2/PB4.
missed.quote: ∀ δ0 ∈ J = Ker(𝒢[0] → M[0]), on a α(δ0), β(δ0) ∈ Ker φ
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It shows Grothendieck already considered GT-like structures on quotients, an idea now developed independently. However, the content on this page is an elementary descent lemma, and the connection is only at the level of motivation.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a routine verification: crossed-homomorphism behaviour under a quotient map and a criterion for descent. Its interest lies only in the context of a GT-type framework on quotients of the PSL2(Z)-completion, which loosely anticipates GT-shadows. Nothing here is a substantive unpublished result.
transcription_corrections: Top '551' is Grothendieck's own pagination (archive page 496).
'dont ils proviennent par surélèvement de u' is likely 'parmi les relèvements de u' or similar (choice of lifts u0 of u).
'implique dépendance pas bien grande' probably reads 'n'en dépendent pas trop, si on pose' (introducing (17)).
'On va l'exprimer cette hypothèse' is probably 'On va expliciter cette hypothèse de façon un peu différente'.
Line (19) ends with 'dans 𝔾' (the image group), not 'dans G'.
'images par φ des quantités α0 etc dans G^π_{·,J}' should read 'dans Ĝ⁺_{0,3}'.
In (20), 'α^Π(δ0), β^Π(δ0)' is probably α^𝒢, β^𝒢 (cf. the α^M notation on the previous page), and the target is 'Ker φ'.
In (16), 'αρ(α)^{-1}' means α·ρ(α)^{-1} with ρ(α) = ραρ^{-1}, i.e. the commutator [α,ρ].
The cocycle comparison is u0' = δ0·u0 (with u0 crossed out around δ0), not u0·δ0.
